# Challenges - Two Modules with the same internal packages (Split Package)

This example creates two modules, called from a third. They export different
packages, but contain a separate, unexported package.

| JAR File      | JAR Type | Loaded As | Dependencies              | Main Method |
| ------------- | -------- | --------- | ------------------------- | :---------: |
| `app.jar`     | Regular  | Named     | `domain.jar, compute.jar` |   **YES**   |
| `domain.jar`  | Regular  | Named     | none                      |     No      |
| `compute.jar` | Regular  | Named     | none                      |     No      |

In this example, both dependency jars contain a utility class with the same
package.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

## Run the example

1. Build the application

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean package
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the JAR file was created and copied to the
   `./target/libs` directory.

   ```shell
   tree --sort=name './target/libs'
   ```

   The application JAR files

   ```
   ./target/libs
   ├── app.jar
   ├── compute.jar
   └── domain.jar

   1 directory, 3 files
   ```

2. List all modules

   List all application modules under `./target/libs`

   ```shell
   java --module-path './target/libs' --list-modules
   ```

3. Describe the JAR files

   Describe the `app.jar`

   ```shell
   jar --describe-module --file './target/libs/app.jar'
   ```

   The application module description

   ```
   demo.app@1.0.0 jar:file:///./target/libs/app.jar!/module-info.class
   requires demo.compute
   requires demo.domain
   requires java.base mandated
   contains demo.app
   main-class demo.app.Main
   ```

   Describe the `compute.jar`

   ```shell
   jar --describe-module --file './target/libs/compute.jar'
   ```

   The compute module description

   ```
   demo.compute@1.0.0 jar:file:///./target/libs/compute.jar!/module-info.class
   exports demo.compute
   requires java.base mandated
   contains demo.util
   ```

   Describe the `domain.jar`

   ```shell
   jar --describe-module --file './target/libs/domain.jar'
   ```

   The domain module description

   ```
   demo.domain@1.0.0 jar:file:///./target/libs/domain.jar!/module-info.class
   exports demo.domain
   requires java.base mandated
   contains demo.util
   ```

4. Run the application

   Run the application using the class path (loading all JAR files as unnamed
   modules)

   ```shell
   java \
     --class-path './target/libs/*' \
     demo.app.Main
   ```

   The application works and prints the following

   ```
   Learn from yesterday, live for today, hope for tomorrow. The important thing is not to stop questioning. by Albert Einstein
   3 * 7 = 21.000000
   3 / 7 = 0.428571
   ```

   Run the application using the module path

   ```shell
   java \
     --module-path './target/libs' \
     --module demo.app
   ```

   The application does not work because the compute and domain modules share a
   package, even though it is not exported and is used only within their
   respective modules.

   ```
   Error occurred during initialization of boot layer
   java.lang.LayerInstantiationException: Package demo.util in both module demo.domain and module demo.compute
   ```
